Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dil . ov_ h s. 2021 OILG OPINION NO. t 02 2024 HON. HECTOR RAQUID LOYOLA Vice Mayor Municipality of Oas Province of Albay Dear Vice Mayor Loyola: This has reference to your letter requesting this Department's legal opinion concerning the scope of the phrase "no other business" under Section 323 of the Local Govemment Code (LGC) specifically on the prohibition of taking up other business. Per the representation, the antecedent facts are as follows: • • The Summary Form 3E of The Local Development Investment Program was submitted to the Sangguniang Bayan of Oas for approval. On January 05, 2023, the Local Development Investment Program of your local govemment unit (LGU) was disapproved through Resolution No. I Series of 2023 for failure to conform with the processes, contents and forms indicated in the guidelines for the formulation of LDIP. The Local Chief Executive failed to submit on time the Local Development Investment Proqram. Annual Investment Proqram and the Local Expenditure Proqram. As a result, your (LGU) had a reenacted budget. You are of the view that since the LCE has yet to submit the proposed Annual Budget, the Sangguniang Bayan may take up other business to attend to its duty and mandate as the legislative body of the LGU. In support of your position, you cited Section 318 of the LGC, specifically second paragraph thereof, which requires that "the local chief executive shall submit the said executive budget to the sanggunian concemed not later than sixteenth (16th) of October of the current fiscal year. " It is your opinion that for Sec. 323 to be operative, Sec. 318 should first be satisfied such that it is only when the LCE shall have submitted the proposed budget that the Sangguniang Bayan shall be covered by the provision stated in Section 323. Hence, the request for clarification. " Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan"

Your position appears to be meritorious. Section 323 reads: SECTION 323. Failure to Enact the Annual Appropriations. - In case the Sanggunian concemed fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appmpnations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. If the Sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is passed by the Sanggunian concemed. However, only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. 138 In the implementation of such reenacted ordinance, the local treasurer concemed shall exclude from the estimates of income for the preceding fiscal year those realized from nonrecurring sources, like national aids, proceeds from loans, sale of assets, prior year adjustments, and other analogous sources of income. No ordinance authorizing supplemental appropriations shall be passed in place of the annual appropriations. In case the revised income estimates be less than the aggregate reenacted appropriations, the local treasurer concemed shall accordingly advise the Sanggunian concemed which shall, within ten (IO) days from the receipt of such advice, make the necessary adjustments or reductions. The revised appropriations authorized by the Sanggunian concemed shall then be the basis for disbursements. Though not explicitly declared, we are of the view that the foregoing provision only takes effect once the proposed budget is with the Sanggunian for consideration and approval. It does not apply, as in this case, when the LCE has yet to submit the proposed budget, as there is nothing for the Sanggunian to consider and deliberate upon. The basis for this is that Section 323 is just one phase of the whole local budget process. Correspondingly, we cite Section 318, 2nd paragraph, and Section 319, of the Local Govemment Code, viz: "SECTION 318. Preparation of the Budget by the Local Chief Executive. xxx The local chief executive shall submit the said executive budget to the Sanggunian concerned not later than the sixteenth (16th) of October of the current fiscal year. xxx" "SECTION 319. Legislative Authorization of the Budget - On or

before the end of the cunent fiscal year, the Sanggunian concerned shall enact, through an ordinance, the annual budget of the local govemment unit for the ensuing fiscal year on the basis of the estimates of income and expenditures submitted by the local chief executive. " The above provisions are further clarified under Step 6, Item 1.5 (Steps in the Budget Preparation Phase), Chapter I of the Budget Operations Manual (BOM) for LGUs issued by the Department of Budget and Management, to wit: "Chapter 1. Budget Preparation Phase xxx 1.5. Steps in Budget Preparation Phase xxx xxx Step 6. Submit Local Expenditure Program, together with the following documents, to the Sanggunian not later than the 16th of October of the current year (Section 318, RA No. 7160) • Budget Message; • Plantilla of Personnel; • Statement of Indebtedness; • Annual Operating Budget of Local Economic Enterprise(s), if any; • Annual Investment Program Evidently, it is the submission of the executive budget to the Sanggunian that sets in motion the participation of the Sanggunian in the said budget as exemplified under Sections 318 and 319 of the LGC. The executive budget is a material document for deliberation and authorization by the Sanggunian. Therefore, the Sanggunian must first receive it from the LCE to evaluate its compliance with budgetary requirements and general limitations. It is recalled here that, as of February 9, 2023, your LCE has yet to submit the Local Executive Program and the Annual Investment Program to the Sangguniang Bayan. To our mind, the non-submission of these budgetary documents precluded the application of Section 323. Therefore, the Department submits that Section 323 of the LGC only applies in case the Sanggunian fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year such that beginning thereon, the Sanggunian is mandated to conduct sessions until the budget ordinance is approved and no other business shall be tackled except the annual budget. In sum, a comparative reading of Sections 318, 319 and 323 contemplates two possible scenarios, to wit: First. timely submission of the executive budqet to the Sanqgunian not later than the sixteenth of October of the current fiscal year. yet it fails to enact the annual budget at the end of the current fiscal year. In such a case, the Sanggunian shall continue to hold sessions at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, without additional remuneration for its members and not take other

business until such ordinance is approved. Second. non-submission of the executive budget to the Sanggunian on or before end of the current fiscal year, in which case the Sangguniang may deliberate and take up other matters without violating the express command of Section 323. Be it noted, however, that in both instances, the concemed LGU shall operate on a reenacted budget if the sanggunian fails to enact the appropriation ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY ATTY.
